title: Token-aware contract autoscaler with safety regulators
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need an autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated fleets that enforces contracted throughput targets (tokens/sec) while minimizing cost and preventing destabilizing scale churn. This ticket proposes a token-aware, contract-first autoscaler that blends predictive demand smoothing with a safety regulator layer that enforces per-fleet bounds and graceful fallback behavior.

Problem: Current autoscalers optimize for single metrics (CPU/replica count or p95 latency) and can overshoot on bursty tokenized workloads or underserve KV-cache-affine workloads. When customers purchase a committed throughput level for Dedicated capacity, we must honor that contract with deterministic, auditable scaling behavior and hard safety limits to avoid SLA breaches and cascading failures.

Goals:
- Honor contracted throughput targets (tokens/sec per-tenant or per-fleet) within a 95% compliance window over rolling 5m windows.
- Avoid oscillation: limit upward and downward slew to configured percent-per-minute and minimum stabilization windows.
- Respect cost/priority tiers: prefer cheaper model variants when capacity is constrained, and provide automatic graceful degradation (reduced max context length or quantized variant) as last-resort fallback.
- Provide observability and deterministic explainability for scaling decisions (why, when, and what changed).

Design overview:
1) Metric surface: the autoscaler will accept a set of target metrics in order of precedence (list): "tokens_per_second", "p95_latency_ms", "successful_requests_per_minute". Each target can be expressed as an absolute target (e.g., 50k tokens/s) or a percentile target (p95 latency < 250ms). The engine synthesizes a composite score via weightings defined per-contract.

2) Hybrid scaling algorithm: predictive + regulator: 
  - Predictive pipeline: lightweight demand forecaster (exponential moving average + seasonality window + tokenization-weighted feature) provides a 1-10 minute forecast of token load. Forecasting uses per-route token length distribution and recent KV-cache hit ratio to estimate effective token generation cost.
  - Reactive governor: a PID-inspired controller acting on composite score (error = target - observed) with configurable integral windup limits. The controller outputs a desired scale delta in instance-equivalents.
  - Commit stage (safety regulator): applies hard limits: min_instances, max_instances, max_scale_pct_per_min, cooldown_seconds, and a surge_buffer_reserve that can be borrowed only if headroom credit available. If constraint violation would occur (e.g., predicted scale exceeds contract max), the regulator clamps the decision and emits an actionable reason code.

3) Token-awareness and KV affinity: scaling decisions are adjusted for cache affinity: requests with high KV-cache hit rates have lower token-cost multipliers. We maintain a short-term per-route token_cost_multiplier that multiplies forecasted tokens when converting to instance needs. This reduces unnecessary scaling for cache-heavy traffic.

4) Graceful degradation: if scaling is insufficient and the regulator detects sustained negative headroom (contract > available capacity for > 30s), the orchestrator executes a configured remediation policy in order: (a) switch routes to compatible smaller model variant, (b) reduce default max_context_tokens for non-critical routes, (c) shed best-effort burst traffic by enabling rate-limits with customer-visible metrics. Each remediation is auditable and reversible.

5) Config schema (customer-facing options):
  - target_metric: string (e.g., "tokens_per_second")
  - contract_target_value: integer (tokens/sec)
  - scaling_algorithm: string ("hybrid_pid_predictive")
  - min_instances: integer
  - max_instances: integer
  - max_scale_pct_per_min: integer (percent)
  - cooldown_seconds: integer
  - surge_buffer_reserve: integer (instance-equivalents)
  - kv_cache_affinity_enabled: boolean
  - fallback_order: list of strings (e.g., ["model_variant_downshift","context_truncate","burst_shedding"])
  - explainability_level: string (none|basic|detailed)

Safety rules and limits:
- Max ramp-up: no more than max_scale_pct_per_min in a single minute (default 40%).
- Max ramp-down: symmetric to ramp-up unless explicitly overridden (default 20%/min when cost-saving mode enabled).
- Integral windup cap: integral term limited to avoid runaway after prolonged error.
- Emergency cap: a global fleet-level cap prevents any single autoscaler from consuming > X% of fleet capacity during transient storms (configurable per-fleet).
- Rollback windows: if a scale action results in increased error rate or p95 latency within 2 minutes, an automatic rollback is triggered and a forensic event is logged.

Observability & auditability:
- Every scale decision writes a structured event (decision_id, timestamp, inputs: forecast/observed/kv_hit_ratio, proposed_delta, clamped_delta, reason_code) to the console event stream and to the dedicated audit log for the customer (retention per contract).
- Dashboards: per-fleet throughput compliance, recent clamped decisions, rollback events, and headroom credit ledger.
- Replay: we record the short window of metrics used to derive the decision so decisions can be replayed in a simulator to verify behavior.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): Enable on non-production internal fleets with read-only telemetry and no automatic scaling (observability-only). Duration: 2 weeks.
- Stage 2 (limited auto): Enable automated scaling for a small set of low-risk customers with circuit breakers and human-in-the-loop override via Console. Duration: 4 weeks.
- Stage 3 (gradual): Broader rollout with default conservative limits, ongoing tuning based on compliance metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Autoscaler keeps contracted throughput within 95% of target over rolling 5m windows for 9 out of 10 test scenarios (synthetic burst, steady high, slow rise, cold-start heavy, cache-heavy).
- No more than 2% of scale actions trigger automatic rollback in 30-day window in canary fleet.
- Observability events provide replayable inputs for every scale decision and are visible in Console within 30s.

Testing and experiments:
- Synthetic load tests: tokenized workload generator with configurable KV hit ratio and token-length distributions.
- Regression scenarios: ensure safety caps avoid cascading scale when multiple tenants burst simultaneously.
- Compare cost: measure per-token cost delta vs existing autoscaler across 48-hour A/B test with internal traffic.

Open tradeoffs and notes:
- Forecast complexity vs latency: we prefer a simple EMA+seasonality model to keep runtime cheap; more advanced models (LSTM/Transformer) could improve headroom but increase infra complexity.
- Config surface: exposing many knobs gives power but creates support overhead. Default profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) will be provided.
- Fallback semantics require coordination with Console/Contracts teams to ensure customers understand degradation paths.

Next steps & immediate tasks:
- Prototype predictive+PID loop in a simulator (Marcos + Priya) — target demo by 2026-03-10.
- Spec event schema and storage (Aisha) and create console widgets for clamped decisions (Console UX).
- Draft customer config UI + API surface in PRD (PM review).
